props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name for the group — "Assigned to", "Contributors". A bare `role="group"` with no label is skipped by most screen readers, so the label is what makes the group announce at all.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars to show before collapsing the rest into a count. `0` means show all.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter applied to every avatar in the group.

ai.summary: A stacked row of avatars, with the ones past `max` collapsed into a named count.
whenToUse: A task, review, or thread shows several people in one row
The list is longer than the space, so the tail becomes a count
The group needs one accessible name, such as 'Assigned to'
whenNotToUse: There is one person — use an Avatar on its own
Each person is separately actionable — use Buttons or Links; a group is not a menu
You need each name announced individually — a group announces one sentence, not five stops
ai.accessibility: `role="group"` with the consumer's `label`, not a `list`: these are people, and a list would announce "list, 5 items" and walk the reader through each one when one sentence is more useful. The overflow is a `<span>` with `aria-label="N more"`, not a fourth avatar — '+3' is not a person and a circle would have no name. Avatars past `max` get `display: none`, which removes them from the accessibility tree, so the group announces exactly what it shows instead of reading five names over three visible ones. Without a `label` the group carries no role at all, because an unnamed `group` is skipped by most screen readers.
knownLimitations: The avatars are slotted `sk-avatar` elements, not a data array — a `people` prop would put name and initials logic in two places
Overlap is a negative `margin-inline-start`, so it mirrors in RTL; nothing is absolutely positioned
The count is recomputed at render time, not observed — adding avatars later requires a re-render
